title: Case 3: suspicious readings
points: Use the separate four-bus DC teaching model.
Compare the fit to readings with error against known simulation truth.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The separate four-bus linear DC model has three unknown voltage angles, measured relative to a reference bus, and eight readings. This DC approximation is not a full AC estimator, malware detector or sensor-authentication system. Synthetic truth is known for the offline classroom comparison only. A residual checks how well the estimate fits the supplied readings; state error checks how far the estimate is from the known teaching truth.
caption: Four-bus DC model. Simulation truth is used only for offline comparison.

title: What the residual measures
points: Weighted least squares (WLS) fits the readings. Residual J measures the mismatch.
The true state is known in this simulation, not in a live control room.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: WLS means weighted least squares: find the state that best fits the readings, giving more influence to readings with smaller stated uncertainty. That weighting does not authenticate a reading. Here J is the residual mismatch statistic, not the voltage case’s penalty score. Its chi-square alarm threshold is about 15.086272 for five residual degrees of freedom at a 1% significance level. This calibration depends on the stated linear model and noise assumptions. An operator does not have the synthetic truth used to calculate the plotted state error. A small J does not establish that the readings are authentic.
caption: A good fit does not authenticate the readings.

title: L8: run two data attacks
points: Run L8 with the default scales.
Compare one biased reading with a coordinated change across readings.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: L8 runs new WLS calculations. An isolated bias changes one reading. The coordinated Hc shift changes readings in a pattern consistent with a different modeled state. This counterexample assumes knowledge of the linear measurement matrix H and access to the modeled unprotected channels. It is a declared defensive teaching model, not evidence of an incident at a utility.

title: L8: read both cyber plots
points: Left: mismatch J and the alarm threshold. Right: error against simulation truth.
A quiet alarm can appear alongside a growing state error.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The left plot uses a symmetric-log scale. The right plot compares the estimate with known synthetic truth. As the coordinated shift grows, the residual stays unchanged while the state error increases. These plots answer different questions; they do not express the same quantity in different units.
caption: Reference L8 plots. State error uses known simulation truth.

title: L8: a coordinated attack escapes the alarm
points: At scale 1, one biased reading gives J=277.50 and an alarm.
The coordinated attack gives J=3.92, no alarm, and 0.02678 rad of state error.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The diagram is a simple scalar illustration of coordinated consistency, not the numerical eight-measurement system. Read the numerical values from L8. A larger false-data shift need not increase the residual when the shift lies in the modeled measurement subspace. The state error is measured in radians; it is available here because this is an offline test with known synthetic truth.
caption: Values from the eight-reading L8 model.

title: Exercise 3: test a small bias
points: Add .10 to ATTACK_SCALES. Predict, then rerun L8.
At scale 0.10, compare J, the alarm flag and state error.
Does no alarm mean the data are correct?
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Allow one minute to predict, two minutes to edit and run, and one minute to report. For isolated bias at scale 0.10, J is about 10.143237, below the 15.086272 threshold. The alarm is False despite nonzero state error. The coordinated residual stays about 3.920222. This added scale remains within the notebook's plot limits.

title: Exercise 3: a small bias can miss the threshold
points: At scale 0.10, J is about 10.14, below the 15.09 alarm threshold.
A quiet alarm alone cannot prove that readings are true.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Separate the two mechanisms. A small isolated bias can stay below a statistical threshold. A coordinated Hc shift can preserve residual consistency by construction. Neither result establishes trusted telemetry. The state-error curve uses offline synthetic truth, not an input available to an online detector.

title: L8: reset before recovery
points: Restore the original attack scales and rerun L8.
L9 uses a separate fixed recovery case.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Explain the boundary before comparing the recovery output. Changing ATTACK_SCALES changes the residual and state-error sweep. It does not change the fixed recovery scenario held inside the demo object.

title: L9: one fixed recovery case
points: Compare the same case with and without readings assumed to be trusted.
Your L8 scale change does not change this case.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The helper uses the fixed run_wls_demo recovery fixture. The cyber object holds both the sweep results and this shared fixed demo. The comparison tests the trust premise under controlled conditions; it is not a controller reacting continuously to each plotted scale.

title: Data trust is an assumption
points: This example assumes three extra angle readings are trustworthy.
Neither WLS nor Llama authenticates them.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The example assumes three protected angle readings determine the three unknown angles, leaving zero residual degrees of freedom. Independent trusted information must come from a justified source outside this numerical calculation. A zero residual in this exactly determined system adds no detection guarantee. Neither a good model fit nor a language-model explanation establishes authenticity.
caption: Three extra angle readings are assumed trustworthy.

title: L9: HOLD or PROPOSE
points: Run all of L9. Read status first.
Then read the proposed injection and the offline violation count.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The two calls use the same fixed fixture and change only protected_available. Without the trusted channels, the result is HOLD. With the assumed trusted set, it is PROPOSE. A proposal is neither an acknowledgment nor a dispatch command.

title: L9: two outcomes
points: Without trusted replacement readings: HOLD.
With assumed trusted readings: PROPOSE, u about 0.121694 p.u., zero offline model violations.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Read the condition column together with the returned state. The PROPOSE outcome depends on the supplied trust assumption and fixed model. The recovery record keeps dispatch=False. It does not use the equipment_dispatch field from the separate L12 readback example.
caption: Reference L9 output for the fixed recovery case, not the edited L8 scale.

title: L9: check the correction
points: A quadratic-program (QP) solver finds the smallest allowed injection that meets the branch limits.
One flow: predicted 0.17000 p.u., offline actual 0.17046 p.u., limit 0.18000 p.u.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: QP means quadratic programming: this numerical solver minimizes a quadratic effort score while enforcing the declared branch limits and a 0.01 p.u. margin. The flexible injection is u=0.1216936673 p.u., balanced by the reference bus. Predicted flow12 is 0.17000 p.u.; the offline actual flow is about 0.17046 p.u., below the 0.18000 p.u. rating. The actual-flow comparison uses synthetic truth for this fixed case. It does not guarantee AC behavior omitted by the model or trustworthy field telemetry.
caption: Fixed L9 correction: compare the predicted branch flow with the offline truth check.

title: A proposal depends on its assumptions
points: Assumed trusted data support the estimate. The solver calculates a correction.
The operator still reviews data trust, model coverage and missing checks.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Do not attribute recovered information or numerical feasibility to confident prose. The workflow can coordinate the estimator, constrained correction and evidence checks. It cannot invent an independent trusted measurement source.
caption: A numerical proposal still needs human review.
